topic: How does the hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balance efficiency and compactness in V-band satellite antenna designs?
consensus_response: The hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balances efficiency and compactness by leveraging high-efficiency SIWs for smaller arrays, mitigating their insertion loss issues through waveguide components. This reduces overall system cost due to reduced performance degradation in larger arrays. However, this hybrid approach introduces additional complexity and potential interference at the transition between SIW and waveguide, impacting design budget in terms of increased fabrication costs and signal integrity issues. MSWG integration can reduce these transitions, enhancing gain and reducing overall loss while minimizing complexity in design and fabrication.
reference_context: A wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links was presented, consisting of microstrip patches, SIWs, and waveguide power dividers. The radiation efficiency of SIW arrays with different sizes was compared by experiment, showing a drastic decrease from 70% to 27.5% as the array size increased from 16 to 32 elements due to high insertion loss.
